post.description:
Write the flag that `CharacterResponse.is_narrative_driven` reads back.

Shaped exactly like `/toggle-use-local-rag` above: the canonical write is
`/character/update`, and this is the legacy URL the Playground already
calls. Porting it removes the split where the flag was written through
Middleman and read through this service.

post.summary: Switch the whole story graph into the character's static context
post.description:
Write the flag core-service reads as NARRATIVE_FULL_GRAPH_CONTEXT.

Off, the character sees only the current section and one hop of lookahead,
rebuilt each turn. On, the whole story map also sits in its static context,
so it can foreshadow and call back instead of only stepping forward. The
per-turn objective is unchanged either way.

Shaped like `/toggle-use-local-rag`: `/character/update` remains the
canonical write, and this is the single-purpose URL the Playground calls.
Unlike the toggles above it is not deprecated — there is no Middleman route
it is standing in for.

post.description:
Mint a session token for an experience.

The token, not the API key, is what the frontend and UE plugin carry for the
rest of the stream's life.

get.description:
Resolve a session token.

Unauthenticated by design — the token is the capability, matching how the UE
plugin calls it. Returns 404 for an unknown or expired token rather than
distinguishing the two, so it cannot be used to probe for live sessions.

post.description:
Ask the matchmaker for a stream VM for this session.

Running out of GPU capacity is an ordinary outcome for a fixed pool, so a
failed allocation is a 503 with the matchmaker's own reason rather than an
error the client has to guess at.

Is the embedding page allowed to render this session's stream?

Deliberately unauthenticated: the frontend calls it before a stream exists,
and the session id is the capability. It answers a boolean and never leaks
the allowlist.

get.description:
Admin read of the deployment-wide allowlist.

Guarded by a shared secret rather than an API key — it is an operator
diagnostic, not a tenant-scoped resource. An unset secret refuses outright
instead of serving the allowlist to anyone who asks.

post.description:
Pixel-streaming quota check.

The UE plugin polls this every few seconds during a session and shows the
"Session Validation Error" popup after three consecutive 404s. Metering is a
SaaS subsystem that on-prem does not ship, so this answers a healthy window
rather than inventing a meter the deployment cannot honour.

ActionEventBatchAccepted.title: ActionEventBatchAccepted
ActionEventBatchAccepted.description:
What the client is told.

`accepted` counts what was queued, not what reached BigQuery. The write is
deliberately out-of-band: a telemetry sink must never hold up the agent
loop, and a client must never change behaviour based on whether we managed
to record its report.

NarrativeDrivenToggleRequest.title: NarrativeDrivenToggleRequest
NarrativeDrivenToggleRequest.description:
Legacy Middleman shape for switching Narrative Design on or off.

The Playground writes this flag through a dedicated toggle route while
reading it back from `CharacterResponse.is_narrative_driven`. Without the
route ported, the write had to stay on Middleman while the read came from
here — the same flag travelling through two services.

NarrativeFullGraphContextToggleRequest.title: NarrativeFullGraphContextToggleRequest
NarrativeFullGraphContextToggleRequest.description:
Switch the whole-story-graph-in-static-context option for one character.

Separate from `NarrativeDrivenToggleRequest`: that one decides whether the
character runs a narrative at all, this one decides how much of it the model
can see at once. Turning this on without narrative enabled is inert.

TemplateListRequest.title: TemplateListRequest
TemplateListRequest.description: Body of POST /functions/templates/list — language filter optional.

TestEnvironmentFixtureCapture.title: TestEnvironmentFixtureCapture
TestEnvironmentFixtureCapture.description:
Where an ``sdk_captured`` fixture came from.

The Playground derives this from a recovered dynamic-prompt template: the
template hash keys deduplication, the observation window and sample count
describe how often the SDK sent that shape, and the source identifiers let
a reviewer find the original interaction.
